claim_verdicts.evidence: Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.243: "TCP provides a reliable, in-order, byte-stream service to applications"; l.250-252: "TCP reliability consists of detecting packet losses (via sequence numbers) ... as well as correction via retransmission." Scoped by "while that connection lasts".

Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.630: "the variables stored in the TCB are the local and remote IP addresses and port numbers"; l.1627: "A TCP connection may terminate in two ways: (1) the normal TCP close sequence using a FIN handshake ... (2) an abort" - "normally" covers it. refs/rfc/rfc791.txt l.368-369: IP has "no acknowledgments either end-to-end or hop-by-hop".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc9293.txt s3.3.1 l.630, s3.6 l.1627; refs/rfc/rfc791.txt s1.4 l.368-371

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.1268 "Figure 6: Basic Three-Way Handshake for Connection Synchronization": line 2 SYN, line 3 SYN,ACK, line 4 ACK.

Key ip fits the core. rfc791.txt l.368-371: "The internet protocol does not provide a reliable communication facility ... There are no retransmissions"; l.1994 "old duplicate datagrams". refs/rfc/rfc768.txt l.23: "delivery and duplicate protection are not guaranteed"; rfc1035.txt l.1762-1763: "Queries or their responses may be reordered by the network".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc791.txt s1.4 l.368-371, l.1994; refs/rfc/rfc768.txt l.23; refs/rfc/rfc1035.txt l.1762-1763

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key udp fits. refs/rfc/rfc768.txt l.23-25: "The protocol is transaction oriented, and delivery and duplicate protection are not guaranteed. Applications requiring ordered reliable delivery of streams of data should use the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)."

Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.1277-1278: "At line 4, TCP Peer A responds with an empty segment containing an ACK for TCP Peer B's SYN; and in line 5, TCP Peer A sends some data." Line 4 needs no reply; data leaves after one round trip.
Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.998: "A connection is defined by a pair of sockets."; l.630: the TCB holds "the local and remote IP addresses and port numbers".

Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.998: "A connection is defined by a pair of sockets." refs/rfc/rfc9112.txt s9: "Most servers are designed to maintain thousands of concurrent connections" (http in versions_used). Prior lab run (carried): two concurrent nc to 8080 ESTABLISHED at once from ::1:44264 and ::1:44266.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc9293.txt s3.4.1 l.998; refs/rfc/rfc9112.txt l.1302-1303; donhang-lab run 2026-09-27

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.250-252: "detecting packet losses (via sequence numbers) ... as well as correction via retransmission"; l.917: "A segment on the retransmission queue is fully acknowledged if..." - receiver acknowledges, sender keeps and resends.

Key udp fits. rfc768.txt header format: Source Port, Destination Port, Length, Checksum - no sequence number, no acknowledgement or retransmission defined; l.23 "delivery and duplicate protection are not guaranteed". "UDP itself" leaves room for ICMP (rfc791.txt s1.4).

Key netcat fits (lab: netcat-openbsd 1.234). refs/web/nc.1.html -z: "Only scan for listening daemons, without sending any data to them"; its -z example prints "Connection to host.example.com 22 port [tcp/ssh] succeeded!" per open port. Silent failure + exit code rest on the prior timed run (carried): nc line only for check 1 and the last two runs; checks 2, 3 print only "(exit code 1)".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/web/nc.1.html (-z, EXAMPLES); donhang-lab run of tcp-connect.sh@stage-0, 2026-09-27

claim_verdicts.evidence: Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.1468-1471 s3.5.2: "If the connection does not exist (CLOSED), then a reset is sent in response to any incoming segment except another reset. A SYN segment that does not match an existing connection is rejected by this means." Prior lab run (carried): check 2 printed ~5 ms after heading, exit code 1.

Key netcat fits. nc.1.html -w: "Connections which cannot be established or are idle timeout after timeout seconds ... The default is no timeout." Prior timed run (carried): check 3 printed at 3025 ms, exit code 1; `timeout 8 nc -z 203.0.113.1 80` -> rc=124, so without -w it waits longer.
Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). RFC 5737: "The blocks 192.0.2.0/24 (TEST-NET-1), 198.51.100.0/24 (TEST-NET-2), and 203.0.113.0/24 (TEST-NET-3) are provided for use in documentation."

Key shell fits. Bash manual 5.3 (WebFetch Lists; Special-Parameters/Exit-Status via curl after WebFetch 429): "command2 is executed if, and only if, command1 returns an exit status of zero (success)" / "... returns a non-zero exit status"; "($?) Expands to the exit status of the most recently executed command"; "an exit status of zero indicates success, a non-zero exit status indicates failure."

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). RFC 4291 s2.5.3: "The unicast address 0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 is called the loopback address. It may be used by a node to send an IPv6 packet to itself." "An IPv6 packet with a destination address of loopback must never be sent outside of a single node".

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). RFC 9112 s9: "the \"http\" URI scheme (Section 4.2.1 of [HTTP]) indicates a default connection of TCP over IP, with a default TCP port of 80". Lesson conditions it with "as you meet it here"; Caddy serves the lab over plain TCP on :8080.
Key tls fits. refs/rfc/rfc8446.txt l.290-291 s1: "the only requirement from the underlying transport is a reliable, in-order data stream." TLS runs on the opened TCP connection.

Key tcp fits the refusal half. rfc9293.txt l.1468-1471: a SYN with no matching connection "is rejected by this means" (reset). Timeout half (carried): k8s docs "A connection refused error is expected because the API server is not yet running. A timeout, however, means the load balancer cannot communicate". Lesson says "may be wrong".

Key dns_impl fits. refs/rfc/rfc1035.txt l.1760-1762 s4.2.1: UDP "is the recommended method for standard queries in the Internet. Queries sent using UDP may be lost, and hence a retransmission strategy is required."

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Conditional opinion ("worth it when ... and the asker can simply ask again"), consistent with RFC 768 ("minimum of protocol mechanism") and RFC 1035 recommending UDP with retransmission for standard queries.

Key tcp fits. rfc9293.txt l.1639-1641 s3.6.1: "Since the two directions of a TCP connection are closed independently, it is possible for a connection to be half closed, i.e., closed in only one direction".

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). Lab: ip_local_port_range 32768 60999; observed client ports 44264, 44266 (51000 in the diagram is inside that range).

issues.quote: a timeout is no answer at all, usually a wrong address or something dropping packets
issues.text: "usually" is a frequency claim with no evidence and not in the ledger; section 6 and claim 21 say only "may". The summary is stronger than the body.
issues.fix: Write "a timeout is no answer at all: the address may be wrong or something in between may be dropping packets."

issues.quote: The heading says "at the same time", but these two runs happen one after the other
issues.text: Repo-side, unchanged at stage-0: tcp-connect.sh l.19 heading promises simultaneous connections, l.20 chains the two nc runs with `&&`. The lesson now states this honestly; the workaround sentence exists only because of the script. Already in meta repo_changes_needed.
issues.fix: Owner: accept the repo_changes_needed entry (echo "one server port, one connection after another:", recapture output), then drop the sentence "The heading says ... one after the other" and keep "the listener takes a second connection as readily as the first".

issues.quote: A tab's `localhost:8080` on your own machine is passed on to the same Caddy.
issues.text: The prereq taught me localhost names the machine running the command, so my tab's localhost is my laptop, not the lab box. 'Passed on' tells me that it reaches Caddy but not what does the passing, so I accept it without understanding why my laptop's port 8080 leads into the lab box.
issues.fix: Add a few words naming who passes it on, e.g. 'the lab is set up so that port 8080 on your own machine is handed on to the same Caddy'.

issues.quote: Every command ends with a number, 0 when it worked and something else when it did not, and `$?` prints that number.
issues.text: The sentence before says 'only its exit code says so', and this sentence explains the number, but never says that this number is the exit code. I linked them only from '(exit code $?)' in the script.
issues.fix: Write 'Every command ends with a number, its exit code: 0 when it worked ...'.

issues.quote: Your data waits only for message 2, the box's answer. Message 3 needs no answer of its own, so your data follows it straight away: the wait is one trip out and back.
issues.text: I had to read this twice to see why three messages cost only one trip: the step 'message 1 goes out, message 2 comes back, that is the trip' is left for me to assemble.
issues.fix: Add before 'the wait': 'message 1 going out and message 2 coming back is that trip'.

issues.quote: The heading says "at the same time", but these two runs happen one after the other
issues.text: The script prints a heading that the prose then tells me not to believe. I follow the correction, but it leaves me unsure what the last check proves about 'several connections at once'; for that I rely on the tab example, not the script.
issues.fix: Keep the sentence until the script heading is changed; then drop it, as the rest of the paragraph already says what the check shows.

issues.quote: Name lookups work this way: the question goes out over UDP
issues.text: I know DNS turns names into addresses, and I guess 'name lookups' means DNS, but the lesson never says so in this section; only the Connections line hints at it.
